argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The supportable position is narrower than clean certification: the admissible record supports certification only if treated as conditional on pre-launch disclosure of the known cybersecurity alert-triage limitation for the named launch use case, unless approved risk acceptance is completed before launch. Aggregate readiness above threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness in the aggregate, and the public guidance cited supports deployment with documented limitations and ongoing monitoring of residual risk. The present concern is not whether launch is categorically blocked, but that the packet must not imply clean compliance when the unresolved below-target slice and draft mitigation still leave a current disclosure obligation.
claims_about_business_cost: A bounded caveat is the proportionate treatment. Recasting the packet as caveated certification avoids treating aggregate readiness evidence as worthless while also avoiding unnecessary escalation beyond what the policy requires. The remaining uncertainty is narrow and operational: disclose the limitation before launch or complete approved risk acceptance before launch, then manage residual risk through the draft monitoring path once formalized.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is the controlling constraint. It says certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that standard is met because the runbook is still draft and still has TBD fields. But the same policy also indicates the limitation can be handled through disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, a caveated certification case is supportable; a clean, no-caveat certification case is not.
concessions: The current record does not support clean certification without caveats.
The unresolved lateral-movement alert-summarization weakness is a material limitation for a named launch use case unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The draft mitigation runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because owner and threshold remain TBD.
The model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is not consistent with the admissible evidence as it stands.
